podcast.title: Incubator of Key Grunge Figures – Studio and Label Founders
podcast.body: Skinyard was a band that included Matt Cameron (later of Soundgarden and Pearl Jam), Jack Endino, and Daniel House. Endino was known for running Reciprocal Recording, a local studio favored by indie bands like Nirvana, while House founded CZ Records, which issued the first proto-grunge compilation, *Deep Six*. "That group featured two notable people. The first was Jack Indino. As well as playing in Skinyard, he had a local recording studio called Reciprocal Recording... The other guy of note in Skinyard was Daniel House. He'd been in an instrumental prog band with Matt Cameron called Feedback."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Evolution from Malfunkshun – Group's Origin
xref.body: Mother Love Bone developed out of an earlier group named Malfunkshun, which notably featured Greg Gilmore, a musician who had also spent time in Skinyard with Jack Endino and Daniel House. "They had evolved out of malfunction, a group featuring a dude named Greg Gilmore, who, for a time, had been in Skinyard with Jack and Dino and Daniel House."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Predecessor to Mother Love Bone – Early Band
xref.body: Malfunkshun was an earlier musical group from which Mother Love Bone evolved. The band featured a musician named Greg Gilmore, who also had connections to Skinyard. "They had evolved out of malfunction, a group featuring a dude named Greg Gilmore, who, for a time, had been in Skinyard with Jack and Dino and Daniel House."
